at æde.explanation: "At æde" means "to eat (of animals)". To say an animal eats, say: "Løven æder kød" (The lion eats meat). For people, use "at spise" (to eat): "Jeg spiser frokost" (I eat lunch). Said about a person, "æde" sounds coarse.

sentence.da: Hunden vil gerne **æde** kødet nu.
sentence.en: The dog would like to eat the meat now.

at ændre.explanation: "At ændre" means "to change or alter". To say someone has a new opinion, say: "Hun har ændret mening" (She has changed her mind). To swap one thing for another, use "at skifte" (to change, to swap): "Jeg skifter dæk" (I change tires).

sentence.da: Vi må **ændre** planen, fordi det regner.
sentence.en: We have to change the plan because it is raining.

at ændre på.explanation: "At ændre på" means "to change something". To ask for permission to change a part, say: "Må jeg ændre på teksten?" (May I change the text?) To become different by itself, use "at ændre sig" (to change): "Vejret ændrer sig" (The weather is changing).

sentence.da: Han vil **ændre på** huset og bygge en altan.
sentence.en: He wants to change the house and build a balcony.

at ændre sig.explanation: "At ændre sig" means "to change". To say a person is different now, say: "Hun har ændret sig meget" (She has changed a lot). To change something else, leave out "sig": "Jeg ændrer planen" (I change the plan).

sentence.da: Vejret vil **ændre sig** i morgen.
sentence.en: The weather will change tomorrow.

at ærgre sig.explanation: "At ærgre sig" means "to be annoyed". To say what annoys you, add "over" (about): "Jeg ærgrer mig over, at jeg kom for sent" (I am annoyed that I was late).

sentence.da: Hun vil **ærgre sig**, hvis hun glemmer billetten.
sentence.en: She will be annoyed if she forgets the ticket.

en æblekage.explanation: "En æblekage" means "an apple dessert". A fact about Denmark: it is made of stewed apple, crumbs and whipped cream layered in a glass. It is built from "æble" (apple) and "kage" (cake), but it is not baked as a cake.

sentence.da: Til dessert serverer vi **æblekage** med flødeskum.
sentence.en: For dessert we serve apple dessert with whipped cream.

en æbleskive.explanation: "En æbleskive" means "an æbleskive", a round, puffy Danish pancake. The name means "apple slice" (æble = apple, skive = slice).

sentence.da: Vi spiser en varm **æbleskive** med sukker og syltetøj.
sentence.en: We eat a warm æbleskive with sugar and jam.

en æggejagt.explanation: "En æggejagt" means "an egg hunt". It is built from "æg" (egg) and "jagt" (hunt).

sentence.da: Børnene leder efter gemte æg i haven under en **æggejagt**.
sentence.en: The children look for hidden eggs in the garden during an egg hunt.

en æggemad.explanation: "En æggemad" means "an egg open sandwich". A fact about Denmark: it is a slice of bread with sliced boiled egg on top. The word "mad" also ends "en ostemad" (a cheese sandwich).

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser jeg en **æggemad** med tomat og rejer.
sentence.en: For lunch, I eat an egg open sandwich with tomato and shrimp.

en ægtefælle.explanation: "En ægtefælle" means "a spouse". It is built from "ægte" (genuine) and "fælle" (companion). To ask for a spouse's name, say: "Hvad er din ægtefælles navn?" (What is your spouse's name?)

sentence.da: Din **ægtefælle** skal også skrive under på formularen.
sentence.en: Your spouse must also sign the form.

en ægtemand.explanation: "En ægtemand" means "a husband". It is built from "ægte" (genuine) and "mand" (man). To say "my husband" in a shorter way, say "min mand": "Min mand er hjemme" (My husband is home).

sentence.da: Min **ægtemand** laver mad i aften.
sentence.en: My husband is cooking tonight.

sentence.da: En **ælling** er en lille and, som følger efter sin mor.
sentence.en: A duckling is a small duck that follows its mother.

en ændring.explanation: "En ændring" means "a change". To say you make a change, use "lave" (to make): "Jeg laver en ændring i planen" (I am making a change in the plan). To swap one thing for another, say "at skifte" (to switch): "at skifte sko" (to change shoes).

sentence.da: Mødet er flyttet til fredag, så der er en **ændring** i planen.
sentence.en: The meeting has been moved to Friday, so there is a change in the plan.

en æske.explanation: "En æske" means "a box". To name what is inside, put it after "æske": "en æske tændstikker" (a box of matches). Do not mix it up with "en kasse" (a crate / large box). For example, "en kasse øl" (a crate of beer).

sentence.da: Hun giver mig en **æske** chokolade.
sentence.en: She gives me a box of chocolates.

et æble.explanation: "Et æble" means "an apple". To name a food made from apples, join "æble" with another word: "æblekage" (apple dessert).

sentence.da: Et **æble** vokser på et træ.
sentence.en: An apple grows on a tree.

et æg.explanation: "Et æg" means "an egg". To say how an egg is cooked, add "kogt" (boiled): "et kogt æg" (a boiled egg). A fried egg has its own word, "et spejlæg" (literally, a mirror egg).

sentence.da: Jeg koger et **æg** til morgenmad.
sentence.en: I boil an egg for breakfast.

et æggebæger.explanation: "Et æggebæger" means "an egg cup". It is built from "æg" (egg) and "bæger" (cup). The word "bæger" is also in "et yoghurtbæger" (a yogurt cup).

sentence.da: Han sætter det kogte æg i et **æggebæger**.
sentence.en: He puts the boiled egg in an egg cup.

et ægtepar.explanation: "Et ægtepar" means "a married couple". To say two people are married: "De er et ægtepar" (They are a married couple). Two people who are together but not married are "et kærestepar" (a couple). For example, "De er et kærestepar" (They are a couple).

sentence.da: Det gamle **ægtepar** går tur hver dag.
sentence.en: The old married couple takes a walk every day.

et ægteskab.explanation: "Et ægteskab" means "a marriage". Do not mix it up with "et bryllup" (a wedding). To talk about the marriage: "Deres ægteskab er lykkeligt" (Their marriage is happy). To talk about the ceremony: "Deres bryllup er i dag" (Their wedding is today).

sentence.da: Deres **ægteskab** har holdt i tyve år.
sentence.en: Their marriage has lasted twenty years.

et ærinde.explanation: "Et ærinde" means "an errand". To say you go out to do one, use "løbe" (to run): "Jeg løber lige et ærinde" (I am just running an errand). To ask why someone has come to a door or desk, it also means "business": "Hvad er dit ærinde?" (What is your business here?)

sentence.da: Jeg har et **ærinde** i byen, så jeg kommer lidt senere.
sentence.en: I have an errand in town, so I will come a little later.

et ærme.explanation: "Et ærme" means "a sleeve". To say you start working hard, use "smøge" (to roll up): "Vi smøger ærmerne op" (We roll up our sleeves).

sentence.da: Trøjen har et **ærme** til hver arm.
sentence.en: The sweater has a sleeve for each arm.

et æsel.explanation: "Et æsel" means "a donkey". To say someone is very stubborn: "Han er stædig som et æsel" (He is as stubborn as a donkey).

sentence.da: Et **æsel** har lange ører og kan bære tunge ting.
sentence.en: A donkey has long ears and can carry heavy things.

ædel.explanation: "Ædel" means "noble". In names of valuable materials, it means "precious". For example, "ædelmetal" (precious metal).

sentence.da: Det var en **ædel** gerning at give sin plads til den gamle mand.
sentence.en: It was a noble deed to give your seat to the old man.

ædru.explanation: "Ædru" means "sober". To warn someone about driving, say: "Kør ikke, hvis du ikke er ædru" (Do not drive if you are not sober).

sentence.da: Han er **ædru**, fordi han ikke har drukket noget i dag.
sentence.en: He is sober because he has not drunk anything today.

ægte.explanation: "Ægte" means "genuine". It is also the first part of "ægtefælle" (spouse) and "ægteskab" (marriage).

sentence.da: Er den her taske af **ægte** læder?
sentence.en: Is this bag made of genuine leather?

ældgammel.explanation: "Ældgammel" means "ancient". It ends in "gammel" (old). To say a custom goes far back in time: "en ældgammel skik" (an ancient custom).

sentence.da: Kirken er en **ældgammel** bygning fra middelalderen.
sentence.en: The church is an ancient building from the Middle Ages.

ældre.explanation: "Ældre" means "elderly". It is also the form of "gammel" (old) that means "older". To talk about elderly people as a group, say "de ældre" (the elderly): "Vi besøger de ældre" (We visit the elderly).

sentence.da: Min bror er **ældre** end mig.
sentence.en: My brother is older than me.

ældst.explanation: "Ældst" means "oldest". It follows the pattern "gammel" (old), "ældre" (older), "ældst" (oldest). To point to one person, say: "Hun er den ældste" (She is the oldest).

sentence.da: Min bror er **ældst** af os.
sentence.en: My brother is the oldest of us.

ære.explanation: "En ære" means "an honor". To say something is done to honor someone, use "til ære for" (in honor of): "en fest til ære for hende" (a party in honor of her).

forms.da: Det er en ære at møde dig
forms.en: It is an honor to meet you

sentence.da: Det er en **ære** at få en pris for sit arbejde.
sentence.en: It is an honor to get a prize for your work.

ærefuld.explanation: "Ærefuld" means "honorable". It is built from "ære" (honor) and "-fuld" (full of).

sentence.da: Han var en **ærefuld** mand, som altid holdt sit ord.
sentence.en: He was an honorable man who always kept his word.

æret.explanation: "Æret" means "honored". To open a speech politely, use the plural "ærede": "Ærede gæster!" (Honored guests!)

sentence.da: Han blev budt velkommen som en **æret** gæst.
sentence.en: He was welcomed as an honored guest.

ærgerlig.explanation: "Ærgerlig" means "unfortunate". To say you are sorry that something did not work out: "Det er ærgerligt, at du ikke kan komme" (It is a shame you cannot come).

sentence.da: Det var en **ærgerlig** misforståelse.
sentence.en: That was an unfortunate misunderstanding.

ærgerrig.explanation: "Ærgerrig" means "ambitious". To say a person is ambitious: "Hun er meget ærgerrig" (She is very ambitious). Do not mix it up with "ærgerlig" (a pity). To say something is a pity: "Det er ærgerligt" (That is a pity).

sentence.da: Hun er **ærgerrig** og vil blive chef inden for fem år.
sentence.en: She is ambitious and wants to become a boss within five years.

ærlig.explanation: "Ærlig" means "honest". To ask someone to tell the truth, say: "Vær ærlig!" (Be honest!) To start a frank remark, say "ærligt talt" (honestly): "Ærligt talt, jeg kan ikke lide det" (Honestly, I do not like it).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne være **ærlig** over for dig.
sentence.en: I would like to be honest with you.

ærlighed.explanation: "Ærlighed" means "honesty". It is the noun for the adjective "ærlig" (honest). For example, "Han er ærlig" (He is honest).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter pris på **ærlighed** hos mine venner.
sentence.en: I appreciate honesty in my friends.

ærter.explanation: "Ærter" means "peas" (one is "en ært"). In Denmark, "gule ærter" (yellow peas) is also the name of a traditional soup. To say you are having that soup, say "Vi skal have gule ærter i aften" (We are having pea soup tonight).

sentence.da: Suppen har grønne **ærter**.
sentence.en: The soup has green peas.
